items.followUp: Write four functions of the pancreas besides producing digestive enzymes.

rubric.why: Recognises the liver’s role in storing carbohydrate as glycogen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the liver stores glycogen.

rubric.why: Identifies the liver’s role in maintaining the level of glucose in the blood.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the liver regulates blood glucose or blood sugar.

rubric.why: Identifies removal or breakdown of harmful substances as a liver function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the liver detoxifies harmful substances.

rubric.why: Recognises that the liver converts excess amino-acid nitrogen into urea.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning urea production by the liver.

rubric.why: Identifies storage of useful nutrients as another function of the liver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the liver stores vitamins or minerals.

modelAnswer: The liver stores glucose in the form of glycogen.
It helps regulate the level of glucose in the blood.
It detoxifies harmful substances, including some drugs and poisons.
It converts excess amino acids into urea.
It stores vitamins and minerals.
Any four of these functions may be written.

items.followUp: Describe two functions of the liver in the metabolism of nutrients.

rubric.why: Identifies the cells being described as white blood cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming white blood cells or leukocytes.

rubric.why: States a distinguishing structural feature of white blood cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that white blood cells have a nucleus.

rubric.why: Describes the action by which some white blood cells destroy invading organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing phagocytosis or engulfing pathogens.

rubric.why: Recognises antibody production as part of the immune defence.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that some white blood cells produce antibodies.

modelAnswer: White blood cells, also called leukocytes, are blood cells that defend the body against infection.
They have a nucleus and are generally larger and fewer in number than red blood cells.
Some white blood cells engulf and digest microbes by phagocytosis.
Lymphocytes produce antibodies that help protect the body against pathogens.

items.followUp: Define a tissue and give one example.

rubric.why: Shows that an organ is made from tissues working together.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an organ is made up of tissues.

rubric.why: Includes the coordinated function that makes the structure an organ.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the tissues work together for a function and giving a suitable example, such as the heart.

modelAnswer: An organ is a structure made of different tissues that work together to perform a specific function.
For example, the heart is an organ that pumps blood.

items.followUp: Name two steps of the biological method used to investigate a biological problem.

rubric.why: Describes the biological method as an organised approach to investigation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as a systematic method or way.

rubric.why: States the purpose of using the method in biology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it is used to investigate or solve biological problems.

modelAnswer: The biological method is a systematic way of investigating and solving biological problems.
It uses steps such as observation, forming a hypothesis, deduction, experimentation and drawing conclusions to develop biological knowledge.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of drawing a conclusion at the end of an investigation?

rubric.why: Recognises reporting results as the concluding step of the investigation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that reporting results is the final or last step.

rubric.why: Explains that results are shared so others can learn about or assess the investigation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that results are communicated, for example in a report or to other scientists.

modelAnswer: Reporting the results is the final step of the biological method.
The scientist communicates the findings and conclusion, usually in a written report or to other scientists, so that the work can be understood and evaluated.

items.followUp: State two differences between plant cells with and without a secondary cell wall.

rubric.why: Identifies the primary wall as relatively thin or flexible and associated with a growing cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct feature of the primary wall, such as being thin, flexible or present during growth.

rubric.why: Identifies the secondary wall as thicker or more rigid and formed after cell growth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct feature of the secondary wall, such as being thick, rigid, lignified or formed after growth.

modelAnswer: The primary cell wall forms while the cell is growing and is relatively thin and flexible.
The secondary cell wall is deposited on the inner side of the primary wall after the cell has stopped growing; it is thicker and often strengthened with lignin.

items.followUp: Define diffusion and give one example of it in living organisms.

rubric.why: Identifies filtration as a separation process.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that filtration separates substances.

rubric.why: Describes the use of a filter or porous medium to separate particles from a fluid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that a fluid passes through a filter while larger or insoluble particles are retained.

modelAnswer: Filtration is the process of separating suspended or insoluble particles from a fluid by passing the mixture through a porous filter.
The fluid passes through the filter, while particles too large to pass through are retained.

items.followUp: Give two examples of how biodiversity benefits people or ecosystems.

rubric.why: Gives a useful resource supplied by diverse living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid resource, such as food, medicines or raw materials.

rubric.why: Explains a role biodiversity plays in maintaining functioning ecosystems.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid ecological benefit, such as ecosystem stability, genetic diversity or pollination.

modelAnswer: Biodiversity provides people with useful resources such as food, medicines and raw materials.
It helps maintain ecological balance and supports stable, functioning ecosystems.
